disease_label_per_paper: Acute chest syndrome in a patient with sickle cell disease, triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection
presentation_summary: Known sickle cell disease diagnosed in infancy with prior vaso-occlusive crises.
Presented with severe abdominal and rib pain 72 hours after arriving in Spain.
Initial hemodynamics and peripheral oxygen saturation were normal and initial chest radiograph had no pleuroparenchymal alteration.
Forty-eight hours after admission she developed fever spikes and acute respiratory failure requiring oxygen escalation.
Repeat chest imaging showed extensive bilateral pulmonary condensations and pleural effusion.

risk_context.source_text_value: Sickle cell disease diagnosed at 9 months due to vaso-occlusive crisis.
Severe abdominal and rib pain at presentation.
SARS-CoV-2 PCR was positive; kept as trigger context rather than direct ACS ranking evidence.

observations.source_text_value: Forty-eight hours after admission she developed fever spikes.
Acute respiratory failure requiring oxygen escalation.
Required a Venturi mask at 8 L/min and later high-flow oxygen.
Extensive bilateral pulmonary condensations on chest radiograph and CT.

course_observations.source_text_value: Peripheral oxygen saturation was normal at initial emergency presentation.
Initial chest radiograph showed no pleuroparenchymal alterations.

quality_warnings: The rankable snapshot is the 48-hour ACS deterioration, not the initially normal chest radiograph.
HbS percentage, SARS-CoV-2 PCR, treatment response, and outcome are preserved outside ranking.
